answer: Resist sybils with threshold-issued identity: no single registrar can mint an identity alone. The signing key is split across independent issuers, and a vertex of standing forms only when a quorum co-signs. Each issuer checks a different proof — work history, stake, liveness — before its share unlocks. A bridge of trust therefore needs several separate approvals, and a vault of forged names stays empty unless an attacker corrupts a quorum at once. Ten thousand fakes need ten thousand colluding quorums, while an honest agent collects one set of signatures cheaply.
